content.text:
I read PR 142 and how chat and artifacts get their tools. Here's what I found. I haven't changed any code yet.

## PR 142: what it does and whether it fits

It has two independent fixes:

1. **Older messages in artifact chat.** Reopening a long artifact chat currently shows only the latest 30 messages. The PR adds "load older" with retry and duplicate removal. **This fits as-is.**
2. **Pages become checked TSX instead of free-form HTML.** Generated Pages run scripts (and load from jsdelivr) with your live financial data in `window.MONEO_DATA`. A prompt injection, such as a transaction description or a Scalable news snippet, could make the designer write a page that navigates to an outside URL with that data. The PR moves Pages to the same QuickJS → checked-tree renderer Home cards use. Old HTML versions stay viewable but inert.

**Localhost-only doesn't make #2 unnecessary.** The leak goes from your browser to the internet, not to your server. AGENTS.md says data may leave only for services you set up. So the risk is just as real on localhost as it was on Vercel.

**The trade-off:** Pages lose arbitrary JS such as free sliders, ECharts and custom inputs. They're limited to Kit charts, tabs and declared month/period/choice controls. Old pages need a rebuild to become interactive again.

**What needs changing to bring it in:**
- Rename the migration `202611050001_…` so it sorts after `202611070003_scalable_trade_cards.sql`.
- Drop the Vercel-era "deploy migration before the app" note. Locally, `npm run setup` applies it.
- Fix one merge conflict, in `docs/artifact-cards-architecture.html`. Everything else merges cleanly.
- Re-run the tests on top of the Scalable work.

## Artifact agent vs chat agent tools

Artifact chat already runs through the same `/api/chat` route (`app/api/chat/route.ts:273` and `:308`). The artifact agent already has every chat tool, including the Scalable reads and the trade cards. The only gap is that **Pages and cards can't show Scalable data**. The designer only sees data from saved queries (`ARTIFACT_SOURCES` in `lib/ai/artifact-data.ts`), and none of those read Scalable. The agent can read your portfolio but can't build a live portfolio page.

**Fix:** add Scalable sources (portfolio, transactions, security quote/chart, watchlist) to the artifact queries, offered only when Scalable is connected. Two decisions:
- **Data on each page open:** use the live Scalable read every time, or the `portfolio` snapshot saved at the last sync (faster, no live call)? I'd use live for quotes and charts and the snapshot for the portfolio.
- **Trading from inside a Page:** I'd say no. Trades stay as chat cards you tap, as agreed in the trading work.

## Showing Scalable tools based on connection and access

- **Connection:** this already works. The `investments_*` tools only exist when there's an active connection and the AI is allowed to see accounts (`route.ts:96`). With no Scalable, the agent gets no Scalable tools. The new artifact sources would use the same check.
- **Full vs read-only:** this is missing. The order and cancel tools appear whenever you mention trading. With read-only access they just return `readOnly`. The access level isn't stored anywhere; it's worked out live by asking Scalable which tools it offers (`tradingAccess` in `lib/scalable/live.ts:22`).
  - **Proposal:** save the access level on the Scalable connection when you connect and on each sync, via a small migration. Add the order and cancel tools only when it's `full`.
  - Make the two Scalable lines in the system prompt (`lib/ai/provider.ts:55-56`) depend on it too: no Scalable lines when it isn't connected, and a "read-only, trading unavailable" line when it's read-only. The voice call uses the same route, so it gets this automatically.
  - I'd recheck the access level on reconnect and on sync rather than on every chat. Checking on every chat adds an extra call to Scalable each time.

## Order I'd suggest

1. Bring in PR 142 with the fixes above.
2. Store the access level and gate the order tools and prompt on it.
3. Add the Scalable artifact sources.

Each would be its own commit.

**Two questions:** are you OK with Pages losing free-form JS in exchange for closing the leak? And for the portfolio on Pages, live data or the last-sync snapshot?

content.thinking:
I'm weighing how parameter changes should reach the card: either a server round trip that reruns the queries and QuickJS, or something that recomputes fast enough for slider dragging. One option is a sandboxed iframe running JS like a page does, which gives full freedom but brings leak risk, many iframes on Home, sizing, and theming problems. I'm also looking at building the controls as local Kit components.

I'm now looking at the Kit slider option: running QuickJS in the browser as wasm on data the server already sent, so changes recompute instantly without exposing data to arbitrary JS. It's safe and consistent in look, though limited to Kit controls and it adds a wasm bundle to Home. The server-round-trip variant is simpler but laggy, so I'm leaning toward the browser-side approach.

I'm checking whether the parent page's CSP can stop the sandboxed iframe from navigating itself to an outside site. My understanding is that a parent's `frame-src 'self'` also covers nested navigations, so an embedding page could block that. What I don't know yet is whether Moneo sets a CSP on its pages, or whether a wrapper frame route would be needed to enforce it.

I'm checking whether frame-src on the parent page would also stop the sandboxed iframe from navigating itself to an outside site, which would mean a wrapper document with that policy and an inner iframe holding the JS and data. Same-origin navigations look harmless, and sandboxing blocks popups and top navigation. WebRTC may still be a residual leak path that CSP doesn't cover, so I'll note that as a remaining risk.

I'm weighing whether the parent's CSP can cover the jsdelivr script side too, since a script URL's query string could carry data out. The CDN logs aren't visible to an attacker, so that risk looks low, but pinning an allowlist of specific packages like echarts or chart.js would tighten it.

I'm settling on the wrapper approach: a parent document with `frame-src 'self'` so the sandboxed script frame can't navigate itself out, sandbox set to allow-scripts only, and a locked-down default policy. Pinning specific libraries to the app's own origin would also tighten the script side, and vendoring them locally would fit the offline requirement better than loading from the CDN.

I'm dropping the TSX pages, the migration, the inert HTML, and the query removal from the frame as things not to take from PR 142. Next I want to check what the artifact route and page content handle, and look at the chat pagination diff.

I've finished the code part, so now I'm turning to the discussion answer and keeping it fairly tight. The Wealth view pulls from Scalable and shows each holding with its name, quantity, price, value and cost basis, plus crypto and cash, the portfolio totals and performance by timeframe, the last eight activity items, and a watchlist of twelve, all as of the most recent sync. The existing `wealth` artifact source already has all of that.

I'm weighing live calls to Scalable against a snapshot taken at sync. Live gives current prices and more data, but every Home card render would hit the service and fail offline or when the login expires. The snapshot is instant and consistent with the Wealth numbers, though it can be up to a day old. I'm leaning toward a hybrid: holdings and totals from the snapshot, live only for quotes and charts, and a manual refresh on the Page.

I'm weighing three ways to make the widget sliders responsive. Option A runs the card module in the browser with local Kit controls, which is instant and stays safe, though it means shipping the wasm to Home. Option B re-renders on the server per change, which is simpler but laggy, and Option C turns cards into iframes, which gives full freedom but is heavy and risky on Home. I'm leaning toward A.

I'm checking the hardening options for Pages, the wrapper frame with a CSP that limits frame sources, and serving the chart libraries locally so they also work offline. WebRTC can still get around CSP in Chrome, so I'll flag that as a residual risk. Then I want to know whether they want this hardening.

content.text:
I've made two commits on a new branch, `t3/artifact-scalable`. Unit tests (1,365) and lint pass. I haven't run the app or a browser test, and nothing is pushed.

- **`4872ce43`: older messages in artifact chat.** This is the only part of PR 142 I took: a long artifact chat now has an "Older messages" button.
- **`03c7e410`: order cards only when Scalable can trade.** Each sync now saves whether the Scalable login has full or read-only access. On read-only, the buy/sell/cancel tools are left out and the agent is told to explain why. Logins that haven't synced since this change keep the tools, which still check with Scalable before showing a card.
  - With no Scalable connected, the agent already got no Scalable tools; that hasn't changed.
  - Chat, artifact chat and voice all go through the same route, so all three get this.
  - **Before you run it:** `npm run setup` has to apply the new migration `202611070004`. Until then, chat will act as if Scalable isn't connected.
  - If you switch Scalable to full access in their app, Moneo only notices at the next sync. That's daily, or "Sync now" on Import.

## What I left out of PR 142

I left out the rewrite of Pages into checked TSX, its migration and the frozen old HTML, since you want Pages to keep JS. One idea from it is worth keeping, though. Pages with JS can still leak your data by sending the page to an outside URL. We can close most of that without losing JS:
- Put the page inside a wrapper whose CSP only allows frames from Moneo itself, so the page can't navigate away.
- Serve the chart libraries from Moneo instead of jsdelivr. Pages would then also work offline.
- One gap no browser setting closes: WebRTC calls in Chrome. That risk is small.

## Sliders in Home widgets

Today a widget's code runs on the server. Each month/period switch asks the server to rebuild it. Three ways to add sliders:

| Option | Good | Bad |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Slider, toggle and number controls; the card's code reruns in your browser** | Instant while dragging, keeps the Moneo look, and the code still can't reach the network | Only these built-in controls, not any JS; the browser has to download the engine (QuickJS, ~1 MB), loaded only by cards that have sliders |
| B. Same controls, but the server rebuilds on each change | Least code | Laggy: every drag reruns the data queries |
| C. Widgets become HTML+JS frames like Pages | Full freedom | One frame per card on Home is heavy, sizing and dark mode get harder, and the leak risk sits on the page you open most |

**I recommend A.** Pages could use the same controls next to their own JS.

## What Wealth has from Scalable

Each sync, Scalable saves:
- **Each holding:** name, shares, price, value and what you paid, saved by date so the value chart has history.
- **Crypto and cash.**
- **Totals:** total, securities, crypto and cash, plus gain per period.
- **The last 8 trades and cash moves, and up to 12 watchlist items.**

Artifacts can already read the holdings through the existing `wealth` source. They can't read the totals, gains, trades or watchlist.

## Live data vs last-sync snapshot

| | Live from Scalable | Last-sync snapshot |
|---|---|---|
| Freshness | Prices right now | Up to a day old (labelled "as of") |
| What's there | Everything: any stock, price charts, news, full trade list | Only what's listed above |
| Speed | 1–3 s on every open, and on every Home visit for widgets | Instant |
| When Scalable is down or the login expired | Shows an error | Still works |
| Matches Wealth and net worth | Can differ | Same numbers |
| Calls to Scalable | Many | None |

**I'd mix them:** portfolio, holdings, totals, trades and watchlist from the snapshot, and live only for stock quotes and charts, which the snapshot doesn't have. Home widgets would use the snapshot only.

**Your call on three things:**
1. The mixed approach for Scalable data in Pages and widgets?
2. Option A for widget sliders?
3. Should I add the Page protection described above?

f=supabase/migrations/202610300004_voice_settings.sql; awk '/function public.save_workspace_preferences/,/\$\$;/' $f > /tmp/rpc.sql 2>/dev/null; python - <<'EOF'
import io,re
src=io.open("supabase/migrations/202610300004_voice_settings.sql",encoding="utf-8").read()
start=src.index("create or replace function public.save_workspace_preferences")
end=src.index("$$;",start)+3
fn=src[start:end]
keys="array['timezone','locale','theme','voice','ai_models','ai_data_scopes','muted_insight_types','summary_cadence','summary_time']"
assert fn.count(keys)==2
# required keys stay the same; the new key is optional so older callers keep working
fn=fn.replace("p_preferences-"+keys, "p_preferences-array['timezone','locale','theme','voice','ai_models','ai_data_scopes','muted_insight_types','summary_cadence','summary_time','artifact_scalable_data']",1)
a="    or jsonb_typeof(p_preferences->'muted_insight_types') is distinct from 'array' then"
assert a in fn
fn=fn.replace(a,"    or jsonb_typeof(p_preferences->'muted_insight_types') is distinct from 'array'\n    or coalesce(p_preferences->>'artifact_scalable_data','snapshot') not in ('snapshot','live') then")
a="summary_cadence,summary_time,updated_at)"
assert fn.count(a)==1
fn=fn.replace(a,"summary_cadence,summary_time,artifact_scalable_data,updated_at)")
a="preferences.summary_cadence,preferences.summary_time,now())"
assert a in fn
fn=fn.replace(a,"preferences.summary_cadence,preferences.summary_time,coalesce(preferences.artifact_scalable_data,'snapshot'),now())")
a="summary_time=excluded.summary_time,updated_at=excluded.updated_at;"
assert a in fn
fn=fn.replace(a,"summary_time=excluded.summary_time,\n      artifact_scalable_data=excluded.artifact_scalable_data,updated_at=excluded.updated_at;")
out="""-- Where artifacts (Pages and Home cards) read Scalable data from: the last sync (default) or Scalable live.
alter table public.workspace_settings add column artifact_scalable_data text not null default 'snapshot',
  add constraint workspace_settings_artifact_scalable_data_check check (artifact_scalable_data in ('snapshot','live'));

-- The new preference is optional, so a caller that does not send it saves the default.
"""+fn+"\n"
io.open("supabase/migrations/202611070005_artifact_scalable_data.sql","w",encoding="utf-8",newline="").write(out)
EOF

+  if auth.uid() is null then raise exception 'Authentication required' using errcode='28000'; end if;
+  if not public.owns_workspace(p_workspace_id) then raise exception 'Workspace not found' using errcode='P0002'; end if;

+  if exists(select 1 from unnest(array['timezone','locale','theme','voice','summary_cadence','summary_time']) key where jsonb_typeof(p_preferences->key) is distinct from 'string')

+    raise exception 'Invalid preference field types' using errcode='22023';
+  if exists(select 1 from jsonb_array_elements(p_preferences->'ai_data_scopes') value where jsonb_typeof(value)<>'string')
+    or exists(select 1 from jsonb_array_elements(p_preferences->'muted_insight_types') value where jsonb_typeof(value)<>'string')
+    or not exists(select 1 from pg_catalog.pg_timezone_names where name=p_preferences->>'timezone') then
+    raise exception 'Invalid timezone or preference list' using errcode='22023';
+  update public.workspaces set display_currency=p_display_currency where id=p_workspace_id;

lines: +import { activeScalableConnection, investmentsPortfolio, investmentsSecurity, investmentsTransactions, investmentsWatchlist, PERIODS, toMinor, type securityInput } from "./live";
+ * Scalable data for artifacts (Pages and Home cards). By default it is what the last sync saved, the same
+ * figures Wealth shows; Settings can switch artifacts to Scalable live. Both give the same shape, so a card
+ * keeps working when the owner flips the setting. `dataFrom` and `syncedAt` say which one it is.
+const live = async <T>(context: Context, read: (mcp: ScalableMcp) => Promise<T>) => {
+  if (!connection) throw new Error("Scalable is not connected");
+  const { data, error } = await context.supabase.from("scalable_connections").select("last_synced_at, portfolio").eq("workspace_id", context.workspace.id)
+  if (!data) throw new Error("Scalable has not synced yet");
+  return { syncedAt: data.last_synced_at as string | null, portfolio: data.portfolio as ScalablePortfolio };
+const percent = (gain: bigint, cost: bigint) => cost > 0n ? Number(gain * 10000n / cost) / 100 : null;
+    const { tradingAccess: _access, ...portfolio } = await live(context, mcp => investmentsPortfolio(mcp));
+    return { dataFrom: "live" as const, syncedAt: null, ...portfolio };
+  const { data, error } = ids.length ? await context.supabase.from("wealth_items").select("name, currency_code, amount_minor::text, quantity_text, unit_price_text, cost_basis_minor::text")
+    .eq("workspace_id", context.workspace.id).eq("kind", "holding").is("removed_at", null).in("id", ids) : { data: [], error: null };
+    const value = BigInt(item.amount_minor), cost = item.cost_basis_minor === null ? null : BigInt(item.cost_basis_minor);
+    return { name: item.name, shares: item.quantity_text, currencyCode: item.currency_code, priceMinor: item.unit_price_text ? toMinor(item.unit_price_text, item.currency_code) : null,
+      valueMinor: item.amount_minor, costMinor: item.cost_basis_minor, gainMinor: cost === null ? null : (value - cost).toString(), gainPercent: cost === null ? null : percent(value - cost, cost) };
+  return { dataFrom: "last_sync" as const, syncedAt, valuedAt: portfolio.valuedAt, currencyCode: portfolio.currency, totalMinor: portfolio.totalMinor,
+    securitiesMinor: portfolio.securitiesMinor, cryptoMinor: portfolio.cryptoMinor, cashMinor: portfolio.cashMinor,

content.content:
First turn on access in Scalable on the web under Profile → Security → Agentic Investing (read-only is enough). Then **Connect Scalable Capital** (on Import or in Settings) opens Scalable's login (with 2FA in the Scalable app). Moneo then reads your holdings, totals and cash daily as wealth records, and shows the portfolio on Accounts. It uses Scalable's official read-only MCP server and needs no keys.

## Connect your bank (optional)

Moneo can sync booked transactions and balances from EU banks (for example Revolut and Commerzbank) through [Enable Banking](https://enablebanking.com). Its restricted mode is free for personal use and covers the accounts you link yourself. Each sync is written as an ordinary import, so it shows in import history and can be reviewed and undone.
